transcribed_question:
1) Identify this organ
2) What is the structure indicated by the pin?
a) Right lungs
b) Right eparterial bronchus

marker.description: Green-headed pin inserted into the hilum of the lung

main_question: Identify the structure indicated by the pin.
main_explanation: The pin indicates a bronchus located superior to the pulmonary artery at the hilum of the right lung, which is the eparterial bronchus (supplying the right upper lobe).

supporting_question.question: Which of the following structures is located inferior to the pulmonary artery at the right lung hilum?
supporting_question.explanation: The right lower lobe bronchus (hyparterial bronchus) passes inferior to the pulmonary artery, whereas the eparterial bronchus passes superior to it.

true_false.statement: The right eparterial bronchus supplies the right upper lobe.
true_false.explanation: The eparterial bronchus is the bronchus that passes over the pulmonary artery and supplies the upper lobe of the right lung.
